headline: GOLD CLOSES SATURDAY AT $4,165, SILVER HOLDS $57 — FOMC COUNTDOWN HITS TEN DAYS
snippet: Gold spot settled near $4,165 per ounce on Saturday October 17, with silver at $57.05, as the October 27-28 FOMC meeting enters its critical 10-day window. The week saw gold sell off sharply on a hot September CPI print before recovering; the metal is now approximately $708 below its January 28 record of $4,873. Silver maintained the critical $54.77 July 2026 correction floor, the technical level multiple analysts identified as essential to the bullish higher-low structure. Housing starts, S&P Global PMI and University of Michigan sentiment — due the week of October 20 — are the proximate catalysts before the rate decision. A Fed pause re-ignites the structural bull; a second hike to 4.00-4.25% is the bearish scenario commercial hedgers have been pricing in by rebuilding short positions for the second consecutive week per the latest COT data.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH CONTROLS RETURN NOVEMBER 10 — SEPARATION, ALLOYS AND MAGNET CHAINS IN EXPANDED CROSSHAIRS
snippet: China's 12-month suspension of its expanded Announcement No. 61 rare earth export controls — paused as part of the May 2025 US-China trade truce — expires November 10, 2026, with no extension announcement from Beijing. Fastmarkets reports that if the controls return in full, they are expected to reach further into the supply chain than April 2025's initial licensing regime: market participants anticipate new coverage of equipment and technology used in rare earth separation, strip alloy production and magnet manufacturing outside China. The April 2025 controls on seven medium and heavy rare earths including dysprosium and yttrium remain in force and have already widened the price gap between Chinese and ex-China supply — a structural tailwind for Western rare earth development stocks. For junior rare earth investors, the next 24 days represent a binary policy event with no clear indication of which way Beijing will lean.

headline: GOLD MINERS BOUNCE 4% AS ANALYSTS CALL 35% CORRECTION 'APPARENTLY COMPLETE'
snippet: Gold mining equities rallied roughly 4% during the week of October 13-17, with most ASX-listed gold producers posting gains of 6-8%, as analysts at Market Matters stated the sector's approximately 35% correction from its 2026 highs 'appears to have been completed.' The firm identifies a confirmed close above the $142 level on GDX as the bullish trigger and sees the $150 area as a likely consolidation zone, with a medium-term target of the $160 area. The bounce follows weeks of structural headwinds: a hot September CPI print, rebuilt commercial short positions in COT data and all-in sustaining costs running at an industry average near $1,785 per ounce — up 16% year-over-year. A confirmed FOMC pause on October 28 is the catalyst analysts say is needed to sustain the reversal.

headline: TECTONIC METALS REPORTS 19 HOLES AT CHICKEN MOUNTAIN — EVERY 2026 HOLE HITS GOLD, MRE TARGETED Q1 2027
snippet: Tectonic Metals (TSX-V: TECT) reported batch assays from 19 holes at the Chicken Mountain intrusion target within its Flat Gold Project in southwestern Alaska on October 15, extending gold mineralization in two priority areas including a deeper zone of Central Corridor 2 now traced below 300 metres vertical depth. The company's 2026 drill program has completed over 22,000 metres year-to-date with assay results pending from 97 additional holes representing nearly 18,000 more metres. Every one of the 206 holes reported to date at Chicken Mountain has intersected gold, and over 60% have ended in mineralization — an exceptional consistency rate for a bulk-tonnage heap-leach target advancing toward a maiden MRE in Q1 2027. This is a separate release from the high-grade Alpha Bowl results reported October 16 (10.7m at 11.8 g/t gold).

headline: COPPER HOLDS $6.62 AS WHITE HOUSE DELAYS REFINED METAL TARIFF RULING — US BUYERS PAY RECORD PREMIUMS
snippet: Copper steadied near $6.62 per pound on October 17 after three consecutive sessions of losses, as the market absorbed the Escondida preliminary deal and hot September CPI data simultaneously. The US refined copper tariff decision — Commerce Department recommended a phased 15% duty starting 2027, rising to 30% in 2028 — remains unresolved at the White House. In the interim, US buyers have paid premiums exceeding $500 per metric tonne over LME prices to lock in supply, and Benchmark Minerals estimated 730,000-830,000 tonnes of copper now sits as economically trapped inventory in US warehouses from pre-tariff stockpiling. A presidential ruling could reset the premium market and reprice the entire domestic copper supply chain; the longer the delay, the more the current premium structure becomes structurally embedded.

headline: MYRIAD URANIUM ACQUIRES 55,013-HA LOS ALTARES IN ARGENTINA'S CERRO SOLO URANIUM DISTRICT
snippet: Myriad Uranium (CSE: MRAD) agreed to acquire 100% of Argentine holding company Buenavida Metales S.A. — owner of the Los Altares uranium project in Chubut Province — from Green Shift Commodities on October 14, paying C$300,000 cash plus 1,571,268 Myriad shares at a deemed price of $0.4455. Los Altares covers 55,013 hectares across 23 mining properties in Argentina's Cerro Solo uranium district, with four granted mining concessions carrying approved Environmental Impact Assessments. Green Shift retains a 2% NSR, half of which Myriad may repurchase for US$1 million. The deal adds a district-scale exploration position at a time when uranium long-term contract prices have broken the 2007 nominal record at $96.50 per pound. Closing is expected mid-November subject to CSE and TSX-V exchange approval.

headline: JAGUAR URANIUM MAIDEN RESOURCE AT LAGUNA SALADA: 4.2M LBS U3O8 INDICATED PLUS 31M LBS VANADIUM CREDIT
snippet: Jaguar Uranium published its maiden NI 43-101 and SEC S-K 1300 compliant mineral resource estimate for the Laguna Salada project in Chubut Province, Argentina on October 13, reporting 4.2 million lbs of Indicated U3O8 and 10.1 million lbs of Inferred — with a significant vanadium credit of 31.1 million lbs Indicated and 57.3 million lbs Inferred V2O5. The estimate covers only about 4.3% of the project's 210,284 ha, suggesting substantial expansion potential. Jaguar holds nearly US$18 million in cash with no debt, providing a funded Phase 1 sonic-drilling and infill program in the Guanaco block. This is the second maiden resource announcement from Argentina's Chubut uranium belt in two weeks and reinforces Argentina's positioning as a Western-aligned source of uranium exploration upside.

headline: MALAYSIA BETS ON RARE EARTHS — PROMINENT INVESTOR BACKS SOUTHERN ALLIANCE MINING'S JOHOR PROJECT
snippet: Southern Alliance Mining's shares surged 10.5% on Bursa Malaysia on October 13 after a prominent investor acquired a stake in the company, which is developing a rare earth project in Johor state as Malaysia positions itself as a globally competitive rare earth processing nation. The move aligns with Malaysia's formal policy ambitions to build rare earth supply chain capacity that competes with Australia and Canada as Western-aligned alternatives to Chinese-dominated processing. The stock move carries disproportionate signal value heading into the November 10 expiry of China's export control suspension: any credible government-backed Asian rare earth initiative strengthens the structural thesis for non-Chinese rare earth investments across the sector.

headline: HOW LONG WILL GOLD MINERS' RALLY LAST? — SUNSHINE PROFITS EXAMINES THE TECHNICAL AND FUNDAMENTAL SETUP
snippet: A Sunshine Profits analysis examines the sustainability of the short-term bounce in gold miners following the sector's severe multi-week correction, noting two structural complications: GDX still faces overhead resistance from broken support levels, and commercial hedgers have rebuilt short positions in the most recent COT data — a configuration that historically limits the duration and magnitude of countertrend rallies. The piece argues that while the bounce could extend further before the October 27-28 FOMC catalyst, the broader corrective structure has not yet been resolved; investors should distinguish between a trading bounce and a trend reversal. A confirmed weekly close above GDX $92 would shift the technical case materially. The analysis is a useful counterweight to the more bullish 'correction complete' calls from other technical services this week.

headline: GOLD TECHNICAL: THREE FOMC SCENARIOS, PRICE LEVELS AND THE $4,148 LINE TRADERS ARE WATCHING
snippet: LiteFinance's updated gold forecast for the week of October 20 identifies $4,148 per ounce as the key near-term support — the level that must hold to keep the bullish thesis intact ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. Analysts model three scenarios: a Fed pause that pushes gold toward the $4,200-$4,250 resistance cluster; a 25 bps hike with dovish guidance that keeps gold range-bound between $4,100 and $4,200; and an unexpectedly hawkish stance that breaks gold through $4,148 toward secondary support at $4,086 — the intraday low tested during the October 14 CPI selloff before the V-shaped recovery. The trading range for next week is set between $6.42 and $6.65 on copper, with similar sideways setups expected in silver pending the first major data release Tuesday.
